issue_context.title: Implement resolvconf -p
issue_context.body:
### Component

resolvectl

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe

resolvectl has a compat interface for resolvconf, the de-facto standard for dns configuration management before sd-resolved. The following excerpts from [resolvconf.8](https://man.archlinux.org/man/resolvconf.8) describe its notion of "private" interfaces:

> resolvconf can mark an interfaces resolv.conf as private.  This means that the name servers listed in that resolv.conf are only used for queries against the domain/search listed in the same file.  This only works when a  local  resolver other than libc is installed.  See resolvconf.conf(5) for how to configure resolvconf to use a local name server and how to remove the private marking.
> [...]
>  **-p** Marks the interface resolv.conf as private.

So far, **-p** has been omitted from the compat implementation of resolvconf in sd-resolved, but it seems to me it could be beneficially mapped to the sd-resolved concept of a default route.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Implement resolvconf -p such that it marks the interface as DefaultRoute=no.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Use the native resolvectl interface.

### The systemd version you checked that didn't have the feature you are asking for

256.5
comments:
FYI, openresolv controls with `-p` whether acquired DNS servers will be used or not:
https://github.com/NetworkConfiguration/openresolv/blob/dba13c383986487abd393d3f3f126938df52f52e/resolvconf.in#L237-L239

review_comments: but shouldn't this continue to fail if you set search domains but not dns server along with it?

Previously, when no domain is specified, the current domains are kept, and only DNS servers are set. That is, only DNS servers can be updated without touching domains. However, we could not update only domains without touching DNS servers. That sounds spurious for me.

Another option is, clear domains when no domain is specified. But, that may break backward compatibility.

After reconsidering about this, typical use case of resolvconf is passing resolv.conf generated by a user or program e.g. DHCP client. Hence, the input should be complete.
So, now I picked the another option, that is, clear domains when nothing specified.
